newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia security chief, communist leader see crisis.
newsitem.headline: Russia security chief, communist leader see crisis.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed and Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov painted a picture of looming instability and chaos as President Boris Yeltsin prepared for heart surgery later this year.

Lebed, known for his blunt, outspoken remarks, told a news conference on Thursday that the decision-making process in the world's largest country had virtually ground to a halt and some regions were teetering on the brink of disaster.
"We are at a dangerous limit, a very dangerous limit. It is not a time to fight. We must get out of the abyss," he said.

Later, in an interview with Russian Public Television, he warned of growing discontent in the army over unpaid wages. "If some serious measures are not taken, we will have a very hot October," he said.

The ominous statement, with its echoes of the revolutionary "Red October" of 1917, came only hours after Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin issued a rallying cry aimed at heading off dissension in his cabinet during Yeltsin's stay in hospital.

Russian Communist Party boss Gennady Zyuganov also predicted troubled times ahead. On a visit to France, he called for Yeltsin to resign and said his own chances of winning any new presidential election were good.

Chernomyrdin, Yeltsin's constitutional stand-in, has roundly dismissed talk of Yeltsin resigning. Doctors say the 65-year-old president is working for two to three hours a day and should make a complete recovery after his bypass surgery.
The operation is due to take place in six to 10 weeks and it will be followed by a recovery period of similar duration.
However, the chief Kremlin doctor said on Thursday that Yeltsin should be back ruling Russia and controlling the strategic nuclear forces again just a day after his surgery.

Asked in an interview on NTV television how long it would be after surgery before Yeltsin had his finger back on the nuclear "button", the head of the presidential medical centre, Sergei Mironov, said: "I think after 24 hours. After he has completely come round from the anaesthetic."
Doctors said on Wednesday Yeltsin was fit enough to have heart surgery but they delayed his planned bypass operation for at least six weeks to improve the chances of success.

Yeltsin will hand over supreme power to Chernomyrdin shortly before the operation. The premier has already assumed Yeltsin's responsibilities for coordinating the work of defence and security ministries.
Lebed, widely regarded as jostling for power with Chernomyrdin in Yeltsin's absence, said decision-making had practically dried up and some parts of Russia faced disaster.
"The will of the state has gone...Many people have adopted a wait-and-see position," the blunt-spoken 46-year-old retired paratroop general said.

But Zyuganov wasted no time in going back on the offensive after his defeat in the July 3 presidential election runoff. He said Yeltsin had secured re-election with misleading promises and by hiding his heart problems.
"If one thinks of the interests of Mr Yeltsin himself, of his family and of Russia, it would be much better for him to resign," Zyuganov told the French Institute for International Relations.
